subject: general
question: A saves 35% of his income. If his income increases by 20.1% and his expenditure increases by 20%, then by what percentage do his savings increase or decrease? (correct to one decimal place)
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Expenditure : Savings = (100 − 35) : 35 = 65 : 35 = 13 : 7

Total units (Income) = 13 + 7 = 20 units

Use weighted average: 20 × 20.1% = 13 × 20% + 7 × x%

402 = 260 + 7x ⇒ 7x = 142

x = 142 ÷ 7 = 20.28...% ≈ 20.3%

**∴ The correct answer is 20.3% increase.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Initial Savings = 35% of Income. Income increase = 20.1%. Expenditure increase = 20%.

Formula: Income = Expenditure + Savings

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5fa742a36dc0ea9426fc9e84c5ba73b320777ffdbe8276735b383c2a3a84d7d.png] 

Let Initial Income = ₹100

⇒ Initial Savings = ₹35

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 − 35 = ₹65

⇒ New Income = 100 + (20.1% of 100) = ₹120.1

⇒ New Expenditure = 65 + (20% of 65) = 65 + 13 = ₹78

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure = 120.1 − 78 = ₹42.1

⇒ Increase in Savings = 42.1 − 35 = ₹7.1

⇒ Percentage Increase = (7.1 ÷ 35) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 710 ÷ 35 = 142 ÷ 7 = 20.285...

⇒ Percentage Increase ≈ 20.3%

**∴ The correct answer is 20.3% increase.**

**__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Relationship

Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any change in two components directly determines the change in the third.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = (Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value × 100.

Weighted Average Trick

Total % Change × Total Ratio = Component1 % Change × Ratio1 + Component2 % Change × Ratio2.
